# Paid, Earned, Shared, Owned Media Explained

Source: https://lowob.com/research/paid-earned-shared-owned-media/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-03-06 · Updated: 2026-11-17
Function: Growth

> Summary: Every channel falls into paid, earned, shared or owned media. Paid is bought, earned is given, shared is borrowed, owned is kept. Research on trust and on publicity versus advertising explains why each does a different job. A working system routes attention from the first three toward owned media, so companies should build the owned layer before rented channels become the whole plan.

Every channel a company can use to reach people falls into one of four kinds of media. Paid is bought, earned is given, shared is borrowed, owned is kept. The model, popularised as PESO by Gini Dietrich of Spin Sucks, is useful because it shows where control and cost sit. Research explains why each does a different job: Nielsen found recommendations from people we know are the most trusted source, and a meta-analysis found publicity outperforms advertising for unfamiliar products. A working system routes attention from the first three toward the owned layer.

The categories are old, but they remain the clearest way to see where control and cost sit. Spin Sucks credits its founder Gini Dietrich with the PESO model, launched formally in 2014; the paid, earned and owned distinction it builds on was in wide use before that, and Nielsen was publishing trust research on it by 2012.

## The four

**Paid media** is attention you buy. Search and social ads, programmatic display and video, sponsored content, paid creator posts, affiliate commissions, clipping programmes. You control the message and the timing; the platform or partner controls the access and the price.

**Earned media** is attention other people give you without payment. Press coverage, reviews, organic mentions, word of mouth, unpaid creator content, podcast invitations. You control none of it directly, which is exactly why it carries trust. It is unpredictable, slow to build, and the cheapest form of credibility available once it arrives.

**Shared media** is attention that happens on social platforms and in communities, where you participate but do not own the space. Spin Sucks' definition is blunt: "Shared media is also known as social media." You control what you post; the platform controls who sees it and can change the rules on a Tuesday.

**Owned media** is attention on property you control. Your website, your email list, your content, your product's own messaging, your events. You control everything except whether anyone shows up, which is the whole challenge of it.

|  | Paid | Earned | Shared | Owned |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Short definition | Bought | Given | Borrowed | Kept |
| You control | Message, timing | Nothing directly | What you post | Almost everything |
| They control | Access, price | Whether and what they say | Reach, ranking, rules | Whether anyone arrives |
| Main cost | Money on a meter | Time, relationships, news | Continuous staff time | Up-front build and upkeep |
| Trust carried | Lowest | Highest | Varies with who shares | Middle |
| When you stop | Stops at once | Persists, decays slowly | Decays | Keeps working if maintained |

## What the evidence says about trust

Nielsen's 2012 analysis of its global trust survey described a continuum running from earned media, the most trusted, through owned to paid, the least. Recommendations from people respondents knew were trusted completely or somewhat by 92%, online consumer opinions by 70% and branded websites by 58%; a majority said they did not trust TV, print, digital or radio ads much or at all. Nielsen's 2021 edition again found recommendations from people they know the most trusted channel, at 89%.

The same analysis showed the categories working together. Paid digital campaigns that drove people to the brand's site, and owned experiences on that site, produced larger effects than paid ads alone. That is the routing argument below, measured.

Academic research adds a condition. Martin Eisend and Franziska Küster's 2011 meta-analysis in the Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science found publicity more effective than advertising on average, driven mainly by its credibility advantage. But the advantage "only holds for products about which recipients lack prior knowledge"; for well-known products, advertising did better. They also found that running publicity and advertising together weakened publicity's effect.

The practical reading: earned media matters most for companies and categories the buyer does not yet know, which describes most emerging-technology firms. Once you are known, paid reach does more of the work.

> Paid is bought, earned is given, shared is borrowed, owned is kept.

## What each actually costs

Paid media costs money on a meter. Its price is set by how many other companies are bidding for the same attention, which is why it is expensive where the crowd is and cheap where it is not.

Earned media costs time, relationships and having something worth saying. It also costs the discipline to accept that it cannot be scheduled. Our guide to [what a press release is for](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-press-release/) covers one of its supporting tools.

Shared media costs staff time continuously and delivers reach that the platform can reduce at will. The Reuters Institute's 2026 trends report cites Chartbeat data showing referrals to news sites from Facebook down 43% and from X down 46% over recent years. News publishers are not typical companies, but they are among the most motivated users of social distribution, and the platforms have been sending them less. It is the category most companies overinvest in relative to what they control.

Owned media costs the most up front (building a list, producing content, maintaining a site) and the least over time, because nothing is rented.

## How they fit together

A working system routes attention from the rented categories toward the owned one. Paid and shared media create the first contact. Earned media supplies the trust. Owned media is where the relationship is kept.

| Starting point | Route | Where it ends |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A creator post (paid or earned) | Links to a page you own that asks for an email address | You can reach that person next year without paying the creator again |
| A press mention (earned) | Republished on your newsroom page (owned), shared on your accounts (shared) | The canonical record sits on your site |
| A programmatic buy (paid) | Drives to a guide (owned) | The guide ranks and is cited for years |
| A community discussion (shared) | Points to a resource on your site | The resource becomes the reference |

Companies that skip the owned layer spend on paid and shared media forever, because they have nowhere to keep what they reach. Our piece on [owned channels](https://lowob.com/research/owned-channels-email-content/) covers how to build that layer, and [demand generation economics](https://lowob.com/research/demand-generation-economics/) covers how to put a cost on each route.

## Why the categories matter more for restricted businesses

For a company in a category the ad platforms review, the paid and shared categories are partly closed: the largest ad platforms may refuse the account, and the social platforms may limit the reach of the content. That leaves the open band of paid media (affiliate, creator, clipping and programmatic), plus earned and owned.

That is not a weak position. It is a position that forces a company to build the two categories most businesses neglect, earned and owned, earlier than its competitors will. Given the Eisend and Küster finding, it is also the right order for a firm buyers do not yet know.

## lowob takeaways

- **Know who controls each channel.** The answer predicts what happens when you stop paying.
- **Use earned media while you are unknown.** Its credibility advantage is largest before buyers know you.
- **Do not over-rely on shared reach.** Platforms change ranking and referral volumes without notice.
- **Route everything to owned.** Every paid, earned or shared contact should have a way to stay in touch.

## Common questions

### What is the PESO model in marketing?

It sorts channels into paid (attention you buy), earned (attention given without payment), shared (attention on social platforms you do not own) and owned (attention on property you control). Spin Sucks founder Gini Dietrich created the model, formally launched in 2014.

### What is the difference between shared and owned media?

Shared media happens on social platforms and communities where you post but the platform controls who sees it. Owned media is your website, email list, content and events, which you control.

### Is earned media more effective than paid advertising?

On average it is more credible, and a 2011 meta-analysis found publicity more effective than advertising, but mainly for products buyers know little about. For familiar products, advertising performed better.

### Which media channels are open to restricted categories like crypto?

Usually affiliate, creator, clipping and programmatic paid media, plus earned and owned media, since large ad and social platforms may refuse or limit them. Policies vary by platform and country.
